Financial statements at iba pang Ipagay na, ang COA ang may sajclau; dito" These requests, according to you, have' no basis in law as you specifically contended that under present conditions, the duties OT the

Appropriations Conunittee is limited on the ioliouving set of duties, which are as follows: "tiyajcin jcung napaglaanan ng tamang pondo ang lahat ng mandatory obligations katulad ng 55% Personal Services, 10% SK Fund, 5% Gender & Development, 5% Calamity Fund, 2% Discretionary Fund at 20% Development Fund at MOOE na kailangan sa pagbuo ng budget". The proper resolution of this case before us hinges on the proper delineation of the duties and obligation of the Punpng Barangay, on the one hand, and Sangguniang Barangay in the prepa ation and enactment or passage of the barangay annual budget, on the 0th r. Sections 330 and 331 of the Local Governm nt Code provide, viz: "SEC. 330. Submission of Detailed Statements of Income and Expenditures for the Barangay Budgets.- On or before the fifteenth (150') day: of September of each year, the barangay treasurer shall submit to the punong barangay a statement covering the estimates of income and expenditures for the ensuing fiscal year, based on a certified statement issued by the city or municipal treasurer covering the estimates of income from local sources for the barangay " "SEC. 331. Preparation of the Barangay Budget.- (a) Upon receipt of the statement of income and expenditures from the barangay treasurer, the punong barangay shall prepare the barangay budget for the ensuing fiscal year in the manner and within the period prescribed in this Title and submit the annual barangay budget to the sangguniang barangay for legislative enactment. (b) The total annual aperopriations for personal services of a barangay for pne (1) fiscal year shall not exceed fifty-five percent (55%) of the total annual income actually realized from local sources during the next preceding fiscal year. (c) The barangay shall likewtse be subject to the same budgetary requirements and limitations hereinabove prescribed. "

There are two main phases in the life cycle of barangay budgets: preparatory phase and the legislative enactment phase. In the preparatory phase, the Punong Barangay essentially prepares the barangay budget based on the statement covering the estimates of income and expenditures submitted by the aran ay Treasurer on or before the 1 5th day of September. The Punong ara ay has until the 1 6th of October to come up with the said budget ropo al. In the preparation of said budget proposal, the Punong Barangay nust omply with the limitation cited and set forth above and, pursuant to Local Government Code, to wit: "SEC. 324. (as amended by RA 8185)

In its legislative enactment phase, the Sanggunian mainly enacts the ordinance or legislative authorization for the disbursement of barangay funds. Before the actual enactment, however, the proposed budget undergoes review and evaluation by the Appropriations Committee within the Sanggunian- While these duties are not so expressly provided under the Code, it is nonetheless vividly summarized in page 61 of the Updated Budget Operations Manual for Local Govern ent Units issued by the Department of Budget and Management, to wit: "4.2 Role of the Committee on Appropriations. The Committee on Approp ations created as one of the standing committfes w thin the Sanggunian, , shall be responsible for coqducti g a preliminary review . and evaluation of the ecutfve budget. For the purpose,' the committee ay cgnduct its own budget hearing and may call upon the local finance committee, and heads of offices or epartments. Thereafter, the committee shall render it recommendation and draft Resolution and O dinanqe to the sanggunian Such report, recommendation and draft proper. Resolution and Ordinanc will tfen serve as the focus of deliberation. " It is further stated that "the provision on budgetary req prescribed by Sections 324 ngguvgan shall ensure that the •rements and general limitations d 3311 are complied with in the proposed budget" (page 63, Ibid) Ergo, it is quite clear tpat the reasons relied upon by the Appropriations Comjnittee Chairm on his 911eged inaction on the proposed budget submitted by. the Punon Barangqy are outside the parameters enunciated in the abovestated rule of the DPM and Qhus, may be considered whimsical, capricious and without gal basi In the meantime, so as not hamper the operation and the delivery of basic services by the barangay, t e Punong Barangay may resort to Section 323 of the Local Government Cod , which provides: Failure to Enact the Annual "SEC. 323. Appropriations.- In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the . ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations

at the beginning of • the ensuing fiscal year, it shall centinug to hold sessions, toithout additional remuneration for its members, such oy-diyugnce gppyoved, and no up such sessions. If the Sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days fcom the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance 'i authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual, obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith." (underlining ours) . Hence, the Punong Barangay can properly disburse barangay funds based on the 2007 budget as a re-enacted budget. On the other hand, the Chairman of the Appropriations Committee and the other Members of the Sangguniang Barangay are hereby reminded of their mandated tasks under the said Section 323 oi the Code, which provides that in case the Sanggunian concerned failed •to pass the ordinance authorizing ethe annual appropriations at the beginning of the fiscal year, it Shail continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved. and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. Compliance with- the above Section 323 is clearly mandatory as can be gleaned from the use of the word "shall". Failure of the Sangguniang Barangay to comply therewith vvouid make them vulnerable to a possible administrative case of dereliction of duty. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter.
